note: Profile-perfect and cash-poor, which is now the dominant pattern in this batch. He clears 'successful' more clearly than anyone else here: sixteen years in corporate sales, now working in financial management and building his own venture, with enough runway to fund 12 to 15 months of living costs. Health is the textbook neglected corner — fitness went entirely to the back burner through COVID and two children and he reached 200 lb. He is the cleanest good-to-great case in the corpus and framed it in the ICP's own words in his first sentence: 'I'm at a good place, just want to take it to the next level.' He is emphatically not deconditioned, with a marathon history, three months of unbroken calisthenics, 11,000 daily steps and 20 lb already lost before anyone sold him anything. Income fails on the affordability test the criterion is actually reaching for: he draws no reliable income at present and was explicit that the amount is outside his plan for the next 12 to 15 months, while confirming he would start immediately if the money were there. That is the fourth prospect in this batch to fit the profile and fail on liquidity, and the second where a real instalment plan might have carried the deal had it not carried a $1,200 premium.
